projects.name: 3.1.4.12 - Integrated climate-resilient transboundary flood risk management in the Drin River basin in the Western Balkans (Montenegro, Albania, North Macedonia)
projects.description:
The objective of the project is to assist the countries in the implementation of an integrated climate-resilient river basin flood risk management (FRM) approach to improve their existing capacity to manage flood risk at regional, national and local levels and to enhance resilience of vulnerable communities to climate-induced floods. The main outcomes of the project are: i) Improved climate risk knowledge and tools for forecasting and floods prevention; ii) strengthened bilateral and regional cooperation for FRM, including EU acquis requirement and iii) structural and non-structural FRM interventions implemented. 
Main focus at country level will be on implementation of the structural measures. In Montenegro, 2 structural interventions will be implemented: i) establishment of full-scale embankment system on Bojana River in Montenegro and ii) development of climate resilient rehabilitation/regulation system of Gračanica River.

projects.name: 2.1.1.56 - Improving pediatric diagnostic in computed tomography examinations; Building Capacity for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Cancer Patients
projects.description:
The project contributes to quality children CT service coverage at the country. The CT system will allow pediatric diagnostic services for the young population of Montenegro and neighbouring countries. Staff will be trained for its use.
In addition, it is necessary to improve nuclear medicine diagnostics by widening the clinical applications of positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) imaging in the staging, following and treatment of patients with cancer. At the moment there is only one clinic for oncology and radiotherapy as well only one centre for nuclear medicine in the whole country (without a PET/CT facility). Currently all our patients who need PET/CT examinations are referred to regional referent centres. It is also necessary to provide special training and education, particularly for the application of PET/CT in oncology indications, as well as education in the domain of radio pharmacists and physics. The management of our clinical centre plans to introduce specific, targeted radionuclide therapy in the near future and PET/CT together with a small cyclotron could have an important value for following patients. The Clinic for Oncology and Radiotherapy has a tradition of well qualified and multidisciplinary staff, and it is also a university centre, ready to transmit acquired knowledge to students and also to colleagues of other specialties. However, the lack of equipment and appropriate training of staff has created a delay in investigations with severe consequences for the outcome of our patients. Taking all of the above mentioned into account and along with the fact our clinical centre is planning some reconstruction in the near future, now is the right moment to provide training for of clinical centre staff in nuclear medicine, with a focus of the future operation of the PET/CT facility. The benefits would be enormous, contributing to the improvement of the healthcare and consequently to the overall health of the population of Montenegro.

projects.name: Strengthening capacities for increasing energy efficiency and reducing air pollution in Pljevlja municipality
projects.description:
The project will focus on designing and implementing tailor made and gender-responsive support programs that will: a) increase energy efficiency of the housing sector (individual and collective housing); b) promote the use of environmentally friendly energy sources for heating the housing sector (individual and collective); c) promote the use of heating systems with a higher degree of energy efficiency, and d) improve municipal administrative capacities in the field of  decarbonization through managing the projects in the field of sustainable energy and climate change. The project will contribute to reduced air pollution in the urban area of Pljevlja municipality, as well as improved well-being of local population 
The overall project objective is to contribute to reduce GHG emissions, which will reduce air pollution in Pljevlja municipality, especially in urban settlements where coal as an energy source is predominantly used for heating in the housing sector. It will be achieved through the development and implementation of an inclusive, , long-term program to subsidize energy efficiency measures, and the development of a local Environment Protection Action Plan that will be followed by establishment of a local unit for sustainable energy and climate projects and local financial mechanisms. Hence, Pljevlja municipality will build gender-aware administrative capacities to create and implement sustainable energy and climate change measures, manage a financial mechanism to subsidize a number of energy efficiency measures for the housing sector, including inter alia thermal insulation on residential facades, installing energy efficient facade joinery and replacing furnaces powered by solid fuels, used for heating etc.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.2 - Enhance energy efficiency and reduction of CO2 emissions enabled in specific sectors.

projects.description: Developed national and local capacity in aggregation and management in Montenegro’s fruit and vegetable sector and worked with retailers to encourage responsible sourcing. The main objective of the project is to support the development of sustainable value chains in the national horticultural sector, through the consolidation of supply and quality upgrading. projects.description:
Objective: to help IPH to carry out activities related to analysis of bioavailability of Fe and Zn in food according to the Nutrition Action Plan of MNE.  Quadrupole Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer for IPH  will be procured to help them analyse micronutrients (namely Fe and Zn) in food.

Adequate nutrition has an important effect on health and quality of life. Nevertheless, the burden of disease associated with poor nutrition continues to grow in Europe. Poor diet, overweight and obesity contribute to a large proportion of noncommunicable diseases (NCD) in the region. Micronutrient deficiencies and overnutrition in children and adults have become two major food security and nutrition concerns across the region, both of which result in reduced human capacity, and productivity losses. Strengthening the capacity of health institutions responsible for conducting research, policy making and decision-making are recognised as priorities in Montenegro’s strategy to address NCD. The Nutrition Action Plan (NAP) of Montenegro is focused on creating an environment that promotes proper nutrition, and priority activities are related to promotion of healthy and proper nutrition throughout life, especially for vulnerable groups at the earliest possible stage, including before and during pregnancy. Food consumption statistics in Montenegro are at an early phases of development, while micronutrient intake and bio monitoring research are scarce, especially research on iron, zinc and iodine. Therefore, public health institutions responsible for research and drafting strategic documents need significant technical and professional capacities to undertake integrated actions on risk factors, prevention and control

projects.name: 2.1.1.57 - Enhancing Capacity of the National Veterinary Laboratory for Detection of Highly Contagious Animal Diseases
projects.description: Infectious animal diseases may be a significant health and socioeconomic problem for one country, as well as for a region, or even the whole world. Some of these diseases are common for humans and animals. Some diseases pose a very serious threat for animal health in the country. Many of these diseases have the strong potential to rapidly spread over large geographic areas. The involvement of national veterinary laboratories in polymerase chain reaction (PCR) diagnostics both in the world and in our country creates the need to strengthen their capacities. Today, veterinary laboratories around the world, in addition to their core work, perform almost the same number of analyses on COVID-19 as medical laboratories. Until now, the IAEA had important role in strengthening their capacities. However, only through continuous capacity building, both technically and in terms of personnel, can we keep pace with the development of diagnostic and biosecurity procedures. There are several goals for this project. The first goal will be establishing the laboratory with improved biosafety and biosecurity management. This objective requires procurement of new equipment, training of people in PCR diagnostics and in the field of biosafety. It also includes strengthening biosecurity measures when dealing with infectious material. Good collaboration among different stakeholders and proactive clarification of their roles and responsibilities should help in the case of emergencies, where first responders need appropriate information, knowledge and skills to provide the most adequate and timely intervention. Another very important goal is to constantly monitor the epidemiological situation and to determine the cause of the infection. One way to tackle this problem is to research genome of the pathogenic agents, namely whole genome sequencing (WGS). The third goal will be the control of vectors and wildlife population, as they are potential carriers transmitting highly contagious animal diseases.

projects.name: Biodiversity Mainstreaming into Sectoral Policies and Practices and Strengthened Protection of Biodiversity Hot-Spots in Montenegro
projects.description: The project is geographically focused on the Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs) of Montenegro and includes various types of intervention and involves both ecosystem protection and work with production sectors, such as tourism, agriculture, and forestry. The Component 1 of the proposed project deals with the management constraints associated with the Protected Area estate, and unprotected biodiversity hotspots. The project will provide for the improved management of the pilot protected areas in order to ensure compliance with the international requirements for protection of valuable biodiversity within KBAs and other international biodiversity hot-spots. Through spatial planning instruments, the project will promote concrete solutions for valuable and threatened BD conservation outside PAs. The Component 2 targets the productive landscapes outside PAs and in the vicinity of KBAs, where the project will address the sectoral threats to biodiversity via mainstreaming of BD-friendly practices and adjust the sectoral development scenarios for tourism, forestry and agriculture to take into account the potential impact on biodiversity. The project will offer assistance to Government in biodiversity-friendly planning for the post-COVID planning for recovery of the tourism sector, will help developing best-practice standards for sustainable tourism and nature-based BD friendly tourism, and support the small-scale tourism business development towards the more offerings of biodiversity-sensitive nature-based tourism products. For the forestry sector, the project will offer best-practice standards for mainstreaming biodiversity-friendly forestry practices, will assist the Government with support and services to private forest owners, and help promote biodiversity-positive entrepreneurship in forestry. For BD mainstreaming in agriculture, the project will support the Government with the introduction of agro-environmental incentives and piloting of agro-environmental measures.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.1 - Climate change and environment targets integrated into national policies, strategies and planning.
